chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Zurays al-Kunasi, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'The people mention that our Euphrates comes out from Paradise. So how is that, when it flows from the West, and springs and valleys pour into it?'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And I hear that for Allah is a Garden which Allah created in the West, and the water of your Euphrates comes out from it. And to it go out the souls of the believers from their graves at every evening.'

So they fall upon its fruits, eat from it, and enjoy themselves therein. They meet and recognize each other. So when dawn rises, they break out from the Garden, and they are in the air between the sky and the earth, flying, going and coming, and they visit their graves when the sun rises. They meet in the air and recognize each other.'

He said: 'And for Allah is a Fire in the East, which He created to settle therein the souls of the disbelievers. They eat from its Zaqqum and drink from its boiling water during their night. So when dawn rises, they break out to a valley in Yemen called Barhout, which is more intense in heat than the fires of the world. Therein they meet and recognize each other. So when it is evening, they return to the Fire. Thus, they are like that until the Day of Judgment.'

He said: I said, 'May Allah keep you well! So what is the state of the Monotheists, the acknowledgers of the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), from the sinning Muslims, who die and have no Imam for them, nor do they recognize your Wilayah?'

So he said: 'As for these, then they are in their graves, not coming out from them. So whoever among them has righteous deeds, and enmity does not appear from him, then a furrow is grooved for him to the Garden which Allah created in the West. So the breeze comes to him from it into his grave until the Day of Judgment. So he meets Allah, and He reckons him by his good deeds and his evil deeds.'

Either to the Garden or to the Fire. So these are paused for the Command of Allah. He said: 'And so Allah deals with the weak-minded, the foolish, the children, and the children of the Muslims who have not reached puberty.'

So as for the Hostiles (Nasibis) from the people of the Qiblah, then a furrow is grooved for them to the Fire which Allah created in the East. So the flames, sparks, smoke, and bursts of boiling water come to them from it until the Day of Judgment.'

Then their destination is to the boiling water, then into the Fire to be heated up. Then it is said to them: 'Wherever you were, you were calling from besides Allah. Where is your Imam whom you took besides the Imam whom Allah made for the people as an Imam?'

key_terms.النُّصَّاب: The Hostiles (specifically those hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: Where does the Euphrates river come from according to Shia hadith, and what happens to souls in the grave at night?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia doctrine of the 'Garden of the World' (Jannat al-Dunya) in the West and the 'Fire of the World' in the East, serving as the physical locus for the intermediate state (Barzakh) where souls of the deceased interact before resurrection. It specifically addresses the theological status of 'Muwakhidun' (believers who died without knowing the Imam) and the 'Nussab' (rivalry against the Ahl al-Bayt), detailing how their souls remain in their graves with a 'tunnel' to these realms, awaiting final judgment based on their deeds. This narrative reinforces the centrality of Imamate in post-mortem spiritual geography, a key distinction in Twelver Shi'ism.
